newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn lower late on BSE talk, export signals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn lower late on BSE talk, export signals.

text.p: CBOT corn futures reached the day's lows in late trading on a wire service report that an Indiana farmer may have died from Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease, a human version of mad cow disease, traders said.
A scare about U.S. beef could cut into consumption of beef and feed, especially corn.
But Indiana health officials said they were not aware of a death related to BSE.
Pressure also came from prospects for lower U.S. corn exports, which this week included confirmation Taiwan would cut back on its imports.

USDA late Monday said Taiwan would import the smallest amount of corn in three years at 5.83 million tonnes, below a previous estimate of 6.33 million tonnes. An outbreak of foot and mouth disease in Taiwan led to the slide in feed needs.
Technicians also said corn was in a technical slide and the early break in the wheat market helped tilt corn even lower by midsession.
At 1234 CDT, corn was three to 4-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with May down 3-3/4 at $2.99. New crop December was down 3-3/4 at $2.83-1/2.
